entry.title: The Retry Storm Problem: Why Your ASP.NET Core API Needs Idempotency Keys
entry.summary:
The Retry Storm Problem: How Idempotency Keys Save Your ASP.NET Core API
Introduction
Every .NET developer knows the frustration of a failed request followed by an automatic retry. But there's a subtler danger: when those retries hit side-effecting endpoints (payment processing, email dispatch, inventory updates), you can end up with duplicate charges, duplicate notifications, or corrupted state. This is the "retry storm" problem—and it's solved with idempotency keys. Consider a mobile client that experiences a brief network glitch while placing an order. The HTTP request times out, the client library retries, and because our API doesn't track whether an operation has already been executed, both attempts succeed. The result: the payment gateway charges the card twice, the noti…

entry.title: CaseMap: Source-Grounded Legal Case Reports You Can Actually Cite
entry.summary:
CaseMap: Source-Grounded Legal Case Reports You Can Actually Cite
Legal research keeps colliding with the same problem: summaries that paraphrase, invent, or bury the page where a fact actually lives. CaseMap is built to do the opposite — turn a case PDF into a report that stays grounded in the source text, with verbatim quotes and page citations, so you can trust and cite what you read. Product: https://casemap.ecocodes.in Showcase: CaseMap on vibecode.law Demo (video): https://youtu.be/hy4J97sSVpI You upload or open a case PDF. CaseMap processes the document and produces a structured case report. Claims in the report are tied back to exact wording and page numbers from the source — not a free-form rewrite. That design choice matters for lawyers, researchers, and anyone who cannot afford a hallucinated holding or a soft paraphrase of a statute excerpt. After processing, CaseMap is built to keep sensitive material browser-local where possible. The goal is useful AI assistance without casually shipping your case files into a black box you cannot audit. Advocates and in-house counsel who need citeable extracts fast Researchers comparing holdings across long judgments Students learning to read cases without losing the page trail Builders exploring source-grounded document AI (not “chat about a PDF” theater) CaseMap started as a community / open-minded build around a hard constraint: do not invent, do not paraphrase away the source. If that constraint matches how you work, the live product is here: → https://casemap.ecocodes.in Feedback, bug reports, and “this citation path broke on my PDF” notes are welcome. Built by Vasim Ahmed Shaikh. Links above are the official CaseMap product and community showcase — use those when you share or cite CaseMap.
